podcast.title: RCA Subsidiary Founded (1953)
podcast.body: Groove Records was established in 1953 as a subsidiary of RCA. It was one of the "fake indie labels" created by major record labels to gain access to the independent R&B distribution networks they had previously been excluded from. "Groove Records was a subsidiary of RCA, set up in 1953."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 49: "Love is Strange" by Mickey and Sylvia

podcast.title: Minor Hit with Piano Red (1955)
podcast.body: Groove Records had a minor hit in 1955 with "Jump Man Jump" by piano player Piano Red, but struggled to achieve significant commercial success afterward until Mickey & Sylvia. "Groove records had had a minor hit in 1955, with the piano player Piano Red and his jump man jump."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 49: "Love is Strange" by Mickey and Sylvia

podcast.title: Closure After Breakthrough Hit
podcast.body: Despite Mickey & Sylvia's "Love Is Strange" becoming a breakthrough hit for the label, RCA controversially decided to close Groove Records. Its acts and producer Valence were transferred to another RCA subsidiary, Vic Records. "But after groove records that had this breakthrough big hit, RCA decided to close the label down and move the acts on the label and their producer Valence to another subsidiary. Vic."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
